newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline, diesel diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline, diesel diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline differentials were steady late Monday, holding onto gains from earlier in the day as traders squared up positions ahead of the final trading day of the year, traders said.
Some selling interest emerged early in the day in low sulphur diesel barrels, but dried up by midday as discussion tapered off in the Chicago and Group Three cash markets.
"Everything is pretty much holding steady, with some firmness in gas," one Chicago-area trader said early in the day. "The market should be slow into the middle of next week."

Traders expected discussion to remain quiet on Tuesday before the New Year's holiday closes the Midwest markets, but saw activity picking up when trade resumes Thursday as January positions are assessed.
"If this afternoon is any indication, tomorrow should be dead," one trader said. "But there could be some activity in January and February barrels when we get back on Thursday."
Chicago unleaded was steady at 3.50/3.25 cents a gallon under NYMEX February unleaded for first-cycle January deliveries and 0.50 cent a gallon weaker for later deliveries, traders said.
Group Three unleaded for late-December deliveries remained bid 3.0 cents a gallon under NYMEX January unleaded, with January deliveries talked 2.50 cents under the print.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was bid 6.75 cents a gallon under the print for December deliveries and 4.75 cents under for early January deliveries.
High sulphur diesel was talked 9.0 cents a gallon under the print for December deliveries in Group Three and 6.50 cents under for January deliveries in Chicago.
